name: MonarchPasswordStrengthMeter
title: PasswordStrengthMeter
wrapsNative: HStack of Capsule segments, Text, and a VStack of rule rows
summary: Shows how strong a password is while it is typed: a four-part bar, the strength in words, and each requirement as met or not met.
whenToUse: Under a new-password field, to guide the person while they type.
whenNotToUse: Not under a sign-in password field. For generic progress use ProgressView with the monarchLinear style.
api: init(password: String, rules: [MonarchPasswordRule] = MonarchPasswordRule.defaults, showsRules: Bool = true, strengthText: ((MonarchPasswordStrength?) -> String)? = nil, rulesLabel: String? = nil, ruleText: ((String, Bool) -> String)? = nil, score: ((String) -> MonarchPasswordStrength)? = nil)
struct MonarchPasswordRule { init(id: String, label: String, test: @escaping @Sendable (String) -> Bool); static var defaults: [MonarchPasswordRule] }

enum MonarchPasswordStrength: Int, Comparable { case veryWeak, weak, fair, good, strong; static func score(_ password: String, rules: [MonarchPasswordRule] = MonarchPasswordRule.defaults) -> MonarchPasswordStrength }

options.name: password
options.description: The password to rate. It is only read.

options.name: rules
options.description: The requirements listed under the bar. An empty list hides the list.

options.name: strengthText
options.description: Replaces the built-in strength line. Receives nil for an empty password.

options.name: rulesLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Password requirements" spoken name of the list.

options.name: ruleText
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken text of a rule. Receives the rule's label and whether it is met.

options.name: score
options.description: A custom strength estimator. By default MonarchPasswordStrength.score(_:rules:).

states.name: empty
states.description: No segment is filled, the line reads "Password strength: Not entered" and no rule is met.

states.name: very weak, weak
states.description: One segment in the danger colour.

states.name: fair
states.description: Two segments in the warning colour.

states.name: good, strong
states.description: Three or four segments in the success colour.

states.name: rule met
states.description: A filled check symbol and the success text colour; otherwise an empty circle and the muted text colour.

appearance: Four capsule segments on the emphasis background colour, filled with the danger, warning or success solid colour. The strength line and unmet rules use the muted text colour.
platformNotes: The same rules, score and texts as the web. Rule tests are Swift closures. Lengths are counted in Unicode scalars, as the web counts code points, so the two agree on the same password. Several closures are optional (strengthText, ruleText, score). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is strengthText.
accessibility: The bar is hidden from VoiceOver; the strength is always in words.
The strength line is announced when it changes.
Each rule is one element read as "Met: …" or "Not met: …".
Met and not met differ by icon as well as colour.
The list is a container named "Password requirements".
Text scales with Dynamic Type; the bar keeps its height.
edgeCases: An empty password scores nothing even with a custom score function.
With no rules, any password that is not empty scores good, or strong from 14 characters.
The default score counts rules, not entropy; pass a stronger estimator through score.
The meter does not announce while the strength stays the same.

examples.title: With a new password
examples.code:
MonarchPasswordInput("Choose a password", text: $password, purpose: .new)
MonarchPasswordStrengthMeter(password: password)

examples.title: Custom rules
examples.setup: @State private var password = "correct horse battery staple"
